newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh 1997 oil output seen at 27 mln T, minister.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh 1997 oil output seen at 27 mln T, minister.

text.p: Kazakh Oil and Gas Minister Nurlan Balgimbayev said on Wednesday the Central Asian nation's oil output for 1997 would increase to 27 million tonnes, up from a projected 24 million tonnes for 1996.

"Next year (1997), we will return to the production levels of Soviet times," Balgimbayev told a news conference in the Kazakh capital Almaty. Kazakh state energy concern Munaigaz said in April that 1995 production totalled 20.6 million tonnes.
Oil production in the former Soviet republic declined during the economic chaos following independence in 1991.
But the Kazakh government is pinning its hopes on western oil firms for the billions of dollars it needs to turn around the country's oil industry which is rich in reserves but poor in technology.

Last week, Kazakhstan, Russia, Oman and eight oil majors signed a $2.0 billion contract to build an oil export pipeline from Kazakhstan's rich Tengiz oil field to Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk which could eventually carry 67 million tonnes of Kazakh oil annually.
